# Kovrent

> Kovrent is a permanent-capital holding company that buys SEC-registered
> RIAs ($100M-$1B AUM) outright from founders with no named successor.
> Part of the price is paid in Kovrent equity, so the founder becomes a
> partner in the holding company. Acquired firms keep their brand (by
> default), team, and own SEC registration. No fund clock. Kovrent does
> not resell. Kovrent is not an RIA.

## Key pages

- [Sell your RIA](https://kovrent.com/sell-your-ria): who we buy and why founders choose us
- [How a deal works](https://kovrent.com/how-a-deal-works): process from first call to close
- [How we pay](https://kovrent.com/how-we-pay): cash, seller equity, and structure
- [What we buy](https://kovrent.com/what-we-buy): the acquisition criteria
- [Why permanent capital](https://kovrent.com/why-permanent-capital): no fund clock, no exit mandate
- [Why Kovrent](https://kovrent.com/why-kovrent): what stays and what changes after a sale
- [About](https://kovrent.com/about): the team and the thesis
- [FAQ](https://kovrent.com/faq): common founder questions
- [Advisors](https://kovrent.com/advisors): for advisors and IARs

## Facts

- Buys: SEC-registered RIAs, $100M-$1B AUM (sweet spot $200M-$600M), owner 55+ with no named successor, off-market
- Model: 100% acquisition, part of the price paid in Kovrent equity, permanent hold, firm keeps its own ADV and brand by default
- Founder becomes a partner in Kovrent with a share of every firm acquired after his own
- Not disclosed: pricing, multiples, fund size, investor terms
- Acquisitions led by a partner with 30 years as an SEC-registered advisor who has acquired and integrated advisory practices into his own firm
- Not: a roll-up, an aggregator, or a fund with an exit timeline
